paper_metadata.title: Composite QDrift-Product Formulas for Quantum and Classical Simulations in Real and Imaginary Time

summary: This paper studies gate-based Hamiltonian simulation via composite QDrift-Trotter product formulas in real and imaginary time, reporting exact numerical gate-count savings on small benchmarks. The largest reported improvement is an 18.8x reduction for 6-site Jellium, with additional gains such as 2.3x for H3 and 3.1x for an 8-spin Heisenberg model, but all results are classical simulations rather than hardware demonstrations.

experiments.description: Numerical evaluation of composite QDrift-Trotter product-formula simulation for real-time Hamiltonian evolution on several benchmark Hamiltonians (Hydrogen-3, Jellium, graph spin model, Heisenberg model), comparing exact gate/exponential counts for standard Trotter, QDrift, and composite channels.

algorithm.optimizer: Gradient-Boosted Regression Trees (GBRT) for partition and NB optimization; binary search on r for minimal error tolerance
algorithm.convergence_criteria: minimum gate cost achieving target trace-distance error tolerance ϵ

key_results: Figure 11 reports an 8-spin Heisenberg weak-coupling benchmark with local composite channels.

The paper states that the composite channel is most efficient, but the localized Trotter channel is not better than standard Trotter, so locality itself does not yet provide an advantage at this small scale.
The authors note that prior work suggests locality advantages may only appear around ~100 sites in stronger-coupling regimes.
